subject: Biology
text: Mitochondria are double-membrane organelles found in most eukaryotic cells. The inner membrane is folded into cristae, which increase the surface area for the electron transport chain. The Krebs cycle takes place in the mitochondrial matrix. Most of the cell's ATP is produced here by oxidative phosphorylation, so mitochondria are called the powerhouses of the cell. Mitochondria contain their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes, and they divide by binary fission. In humans, mitochondria are inherited from the mother through the egg cell.

probes.q: Where in the mitochondrion does the Krebs cycle take place?
How is the mitochondrion inherited in humans?
How many base pairs does the human mitochondrial genome contain?

subject: Chemistry
text: The pH of a solution is defined as pH = -log10[H+], where [H+] is the hydrogen ion concentration in moles per litre. At 25 degrees C a neutral solution has pH 7, acids have pH below 7 and bases have pH above 7. A strong acid such as hydrochloric acid dissociates completely in water, so a 0.1 M solution has pH 1. A weak acid such as ethanoic acid dissociates only partly. A buffer solution resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.

probes.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25 degrees C?
What is the pH of 0.1 M hydrochloric acid?
What is the boiling point of concentrated sulfuric acid?

subject: Physics
text: Newton's second law states that the net force on an object equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration, F = ma. The SI unit of force is the newton, which is one kilogram metre per second squared. Linear momentum is the product of mass and velocity, p = mv. Newton's third law says that when one body exerts a force on another, the second exerts an equal and opposite force on the first. These two forces act on different bodies, so they never cancel each other.

probes.q: On which bodies do the action and reaction forces of Newton's third law act?
What is the numerical value of the universal gravitational constant G?

subject: Biology
text: Photosynthesis has two stages. The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast. They split water, release oxygen, and make ATP and NADPH. The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma. It uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into sugar, and the enzyme that fixes carbon dioxide is RuBisCO. Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.

probes.q: Which enzyme fixes carbon dioxide in the Calvin cycle?
Where do the light-dependent reactions take place?
How many chloroplasts does an average mesophyll cell contain?

subject: Chemistry
text: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. Alkenes contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond and have the general formula CnH2n. Alkynes contain a carbon-carbon triple bond and have the general formula CnH2n-2. Members of a homologous series have the same functional group and differ by a CH2 unit. Alkenes decolourise bromine water, which is used as a test for unsaturation.

probes.q: What is the general formula of the alkynes?
Which reagent is used to test for unsaturation in alkenes?
What is the melting point of ethene?

subject: Biology
text: Mendel's law of segregation states that the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation, so each gamete receives one allele. A dominant allele masks the effect of a recessive allele in a heterozygote. A cross between two heterozygous parents (Tt x Tt) gives offspring in the genotype ratio 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt and the phenotype ratio 3 dominant : 1 recessive. The law of independent assortment says that alleles of different genes are inherited independently when the genes are on different chromosomes.

probes.q: What phenotype ratio results from a Tt x Tt cross?
What does the law of segregation state?
On which chromosome is the cystic fibrosis gene located?
